question.text: A potential barrier of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> exists across a p-n junction. An electron enters the junction from the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>-side with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The speed with which electron enters the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> side will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____.: (Given mass of electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>31</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, charge on electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>.)

solution.text:
Applying conservation of energy

-eVn+12mvi2=-eVp+12mvf2

We know, Vn-Vp=potential barrier=0.4 V

Then, we have, -eVn-Vp+12mvi2=12mvf2

⇒-1.6×10-19×0.4+12×9×10-31×36×1010=12×9×10-31 vf2

⇒-0.64×10-19+1.62×10-19=12×9×10-31vf2

⇒0.98×10-19=4.5×10-31vf2

⇒vf2=0.98×10124.5

⇒vf=0.466666×106

=4.6666×105 m s-1=143×105 m s-1
